title: Burst credit orchestrator with time-windowed throughput guarantees
creator: Maya Gonzalez
description: Problem: Dedicated pools currently provide conservative per-tenant throughput reservations and blunt autoscaling policies that either waste headroom or cause hard rejections during short bursts. This ticket proposes a burst-credit orchestrator that lets tenants accumulate short-term burst capacity within a sliding time window and consumes credits on demand to honor latency SLOs without permanently inflating reserved throughput. Goals: 1) allow bounded short bursts beyond steady reservations, 2) avoid long-tail rejections by smoothing admission via elastic credit consumption, 3) integrate with autoscaler hints so long sustained usage triggers gradual capacity growth, and 4) provide clear accounting for billing and debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by Platform and Runtime leads
Prototype integrated into admission path and feature-flagged in staging
End-to-end benchmarks showing <5% latency increase at p95 for bursty traces while reducing permanent reserved slots by >=15% on test workload
Autoscaler receives and acts on sustained credit depletion signals without creating oscillations (basic stability tests pass)
Customer-facing metrics and explanations added to Console (per-tenant credit balance, burn rate, time-window config)
notes: Spike notebooks with trace replay and synthetic workloads: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/burst-credit-spike
Initial kernel-level risk analysis: small SLO exposure window when credits exhaust; plan to fall back to nearest compatible model variant
Billing note: credits converted to transient usage units for metering; collection design TBD with Billing team
Trade-offs considered: per-tenant credit state increases control-plane complexity vs. global token-bucket which was unfair to multi-tenant usage patterns
